channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Almost 96% of Australian vapes are bought illegally as pharmacy model struggles, research suggests
item.description: When almost all vapes are bought outside the legal system, the problem is no longer consumer behaviour alone. It is a sign that Australia’s pharmacy model is failing to meet demand, leaving people to rely on informal markets with weaker safeguards and less oversight. A system designed to control vaping has instead pushed it beyond control. Harm reduction works better when legal access is realistic, regulated and easier than the illicit alternative. (Published on August 14, 2026byclearingtheair.eu)

item.title: NHS goes "merchant of doubt" on vaping as an alternative to smoking
item.description: A smoker looking for NHS advice deserves clarity, not mixed signals. Vaping carries uncertainty, but cigarettes carry a far greater and well-established burden of harm. Presenting caution without proportion can make the lower-risk option seem too doubtful to trust. Public health guidance should help people understand the direction of risk clearly enough to act on it. (Published on August 14, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: New Research Blows Up the Myths Driving Vaping Bans
item.description: Vaping bans are often built on claims that sound settled but weaken under closer scrutiny. New research challenges the assumptions used to justify prohibition, especially around youth use, switching and the role of flavours for adults who smoke. Evidence should be allowed to disturb comfortable policy narratives. Public health cannot reduce harm by defending myths that make lower-risk alternatives harder to access. (Published on August 14, 2026bythewellnews.com)
